prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (operational name: Juniper) is the region’s primary dispatch and coordination point. It intakes emergency medical requests, supports triage, dispatches ambulances, coordinates jurisdictions, and maintains a shared picture of incidents, available units, and access constraints. It translates reported emergencies into prioritized incidents and responses under approved clinical and jurisdictional protocols. Actors/elements: Call Taker Mara obtains essential details, confirms location, and enters requests for assessment. Triage Supervisor reviews information, assigns/confirms priority, and directs additional clinical review. Regional Medical Director establishes clinical triage policies and limits of protocol-based decisions. Dispatch personnel apply approved protocols and seek clinical guidance outside delegated authority. Shift Commander (call sign: Sundial) coordinates operations, continuity, conflicts, and surge priorities, escalating beyond-center decisions to jurisdictional leadership; does not supersede Regional Medical Director clinical authority or Paramedic Crew scene-level judgment. Paramedic Crew assesses and cares for patients within scope and protocols. Radio Coordinator (call sign: Mistral) monitors Regional Radio Network, maintains clear communications among dispatch personnel and ambulance crews, confirms assigned channels and backup procedures at shift start, and conducts coverage checks in weak-signal areas to identify problems. Ambulance Unit 417 participates in the regional response pool when assigned. Fleet Maintenance Cell (call sign: Bluejay) monitors vehicle availability, scheduled service, and defects affecting zone coverage; produces Battery Swap Voucher for authorized battery replacement. Data Quality Officer reviews dispatch records for completeness, consistency, and information-handling compliance. Participating jurisdictions retain resource ownership and local policy responsibility; regional service coordinates agreed responses. Systems/items: Ambulance Coordination Platform provides incident, unit-assignment, and resource status views. Computer Aided Dispatch Console is the primary incident-entry, assessment, and dispatch workstation. Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates receiving-capacity/destination awareness; Emergency Department communicates receiving considerations through regional procedures. Riverside Trauma Center is a designated destination assessed for availability and suitability. North Gate Status Board presents northern access/queue conditions and produces North Approach Queue Snapshot; South Gate Status Board presents southern access conditions, including ambulance-entry restrictions. Operations/requirements: Operating area is divided into response zones reflecting distance, road access, and ambulance capacity. Zone boundaries are maintained with jurisdictions and reviewed when roads, population, or agreements change. Each zone has primary and alternate routes to the Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center, subject to clinical direction and current access. Dispatch considers travel time, restrictions, weather, and closures for routing/arrival estimates; crews verify rapidly changing access

New part:
S044: The Ambulance Coordination Platform provides a shared operational view of zone coverage and unit availability.
S045: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports dispatch work, while operational staff remain responsible for verifying that displayed information is current.
S046: The Shift Commander reviews readiness concerns that may require repositioning resources or adjusting local coverage plans.
S047: The Triage Supervisor coordinates clinical prioritization with dispatch operations when demand or access conditions change.
S048: The Paramedic Crew reports new access barriers and vehicle readiness concerns through established communications procedures.
S049: The Regional Dispatch Center compares reported conditions with current zone coverage and escalates unresolved readiness gaps to the appropriate operational lead.
S050: Readiness status is reassessed after significant incidents, service interruptions, or changes to routes and access conditions.
S051: The Regional Dispatch Center handles incoming emergency calls through a controlled intake process that creates an incident record for coordination.
S052: Call Taker Mara is also known by the radio alias Larkspur.
S053: The Hospital Liaison Desk is also known by the coordination alias Kestrel.
S054: Call Taker Mara establishes the caller's location before collecting medical details.
S055: Call Taker Mara asks for the street address, municipality, and any building, floor, or entrance information needed to find the patient.
S056: Call Taker Mara confirms the location by repeating the address and checking it against the caller's description of nearby landmarks.
S057: Call Taker Mara asks whether the caller can provide a callback number in case the connection is lost.
S058: Call Taker Mara gathers the patient's age, level of consciousness, breathing status, and the main reason emergency help is needed.
S059: Call Taker Mara uses direct questions to distinguish observed symptoms from information reported by someone else.
S060: Call Taker Mara records the time symptoms began when the caller can provide a reliable estimate.
S061: Call Taker Mara notes access barriers such as locked entrances, restricted roads, or difficulty reaching the patient.
S062: Call Taker Mara produces the Caller Location Correction Slip when the caller's address needs documented clarification.
S063: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks entered location details against available address and map data.
S064: If the location does not resolve cleanly, Call Taker Mara asks focused follow-up questions and updates the incident record.
S065: Call Taker Mara remains engaged with the caller when further information could change the response priority or access plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
